content:
This is sort of a tips and tricks question. I wanted to know how people find the right files in Mathlib to import when they are working on a Lean project?

I sometimes just end up importing the whole of Mathlib or maybe even Mathlib.Tactic. But, I see that a lot of people do not do that, and instead find the right file and import that (does importing something like Mathlib slow the code down?).

So, for someone who has not spent years studying Mathlib, how do I find the right file easily?
You can always import Mathlib first, get started working, and then use #min_imports.
Oh. I do not know about #min_imports. Where can I read up on it and find out how to use it?
Well that didn't work, I'm very sad. Here's a link
The TLDR is just write #min_imports at the end of your file, and see what it gives you
if you feel that import Mathlib is too slow, you can use the module system which ought to speed things up (i.e. write module at the top of your file)
Thanks. Is #min_imports optimal? Like, I just tried it with my code, and it told me to import two files. But, after just importing one, the code worked fine.
No, it's a best effort thing, but I never inspected the details.
It is theoretically optimal, but there are known shortcomings (especially since the adoption of the module system) that are yet to be addressed
What is the module system? It was mentioned above as well. I did not entirely understand that.

Basically a file can distinguish between public and private declarations (declarations that get exported and declarations that don't), see the language manual:
https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Source-Files-and-Modules/#module-scopes

#min_imports worked very well on my project. But, when I tried it out in silly small files, it gave me nothing. For instance, I tried the following on https://live.lean-lang.org/

import Mathlib

example (a : ℕ) : a + a  = a + a := rfl

#min_imports

I expected it to give me something like import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Basic, but it gave me absolutely nothing. I don't understand why. Is it a problem with the website, or with the code (I don't have my laptop on me to check it there)?
examples are ignored by #min_imports, since they don't add anything to the environment (which is the source of truth for #min_imports
